Think of two different people in your community. Why is water conservation important to each of them? For instance, a farmer may have some reasons that are different from some of the reasons a hospital worker may have.

Type your answer in the box below. If you would also like to draw a sketch to express your ideas, use the sketch box (or pencil and paper).

(Optional) Feel free to use this sentence starter:

________ should conserve water because ______________

tiles.title: Who should conserve water in our community? Why is water conservation important to that person?

text:
Today's Activity: Identifying Stakeholders

You just identified some of your stakeholders!

Stakeholders are those who care about your design problem and eventual solution or will be affected by it in some way. In this case, stakeholders are those in your community that you will affect if you create a design solution for water conservation. They have a stake in your design solution.

Stakeholders vary in size and type. Individuals can be stakeholders, but groups like organizations and populations can also be stakeholders. Stakeholders also aren’t necessarily human: plants and animals can be considered stakeholders.

A design solution can affect many stakeholders:

  • those that care about the design solution
  • those that use the design solution (even if they don't care about it very much)
  • those that want the design solution in their community (even if they might not use it)
  • those that might not want the design solution in their community
  • those that will give money, time, or other resources to create the design solution
